keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 649 k km2 for 661-665 reaches 53 N and 9.5 E (Belgium, Germany): that is the Frankish heartland, which Cliopatria otherwise gives to 'Kingdom of the Franks' as a 137 km2 sliver in the same years. The Duchy page has the duchy's first duke Felix ruling 'from about 660' as 'a quasi-independent realm within the Frankish empire' and names no territory; the Odo page's 'Loire to the Pyrenees' (c.700) is the nearest statement, so the 674 shape is used.

Unchanged shape; Lupus 'ruling autonomously (princeps)' and Odo 'certainly by 700' (Duchy and Odo pages) give no territorial change.

Unchanged shape. 718 is the year Odo raised 'an army of Basques' as ally of Chilperic II and Ragenfrid and handed Chilperic and the treasure to Charles Martel after Soissons (Odo page); no land changed. 721: Odo beat the Umayyads at Toulouse (9 June).

The pages say otherwise: Odo accepted 'formal Frankish overlordship' in 732 (Odo page), but 'Hunald, who reverted to former independence' (Duchy page) and was attacked in 735 and 736, and 'Hunald retired to a monastery' leaving Waifer (no year). The duchy is kept, under overlordship in 732-734 and contested at Bourges and Limoges in 735-736.
Unchanged shape for 750-754. The page gives no year for Waifer's accession or for the end of Hunald; Cliopatria's resumption in 750 is not dated by the pages opened.
Unchanged shape. 759: 'the full occupation of Septimania' by Pepin, then 'a cyclical military campaign that lasted for eight years, i.e. the War of Aquitaine' (Duchy page): ledger 760-768.
Unchanged shape in the middle of the War of Aquitaine; the page names no town taken, only that 'Pepin's forces destroyed up to 36 monasteries'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 781-844: Cliopatria has nothing for 768-887 and draws the land in 'Kingdom of the Franks' (and 'Duchy of Gascony' 768-824 as a separate 56 k to 9 k km2 shape). 'In 781, Charlemagne made his third son Louis ... king of Aquitaine. It included not only Aquitaine proper, but also Gothia, Vasconia (Gascony) and the Carolingian possessions in Spain', 'subordinated to the Carolingian king or (later) emperor'. Overlaps the Duchy of Gascony row (flag for its group). The page's infobox is the duchy's and gives no area.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 845-877: after the 845 treaty 'the kingdom had been diminished by the loss of Poitou, Saintonge, and Angoumois in the northwest of the region, which had been given to Rainulf I, count of Poitiers'. 877: 'Aquitaine was fully absorbed into the Frankish crown' (Kingdom page). The Aquitaine page says the kingdom 'ceased to have any relevance' after Verdun (843); the Kingdom page keeps Pepin II in possession 845-852 and kings to 877, which this follows.

204 k km2 (France only, 2.2 W to 4.7 E): the 'new Duchy of Aquitaine, including the three districts already mentioned' held by Rainulf's successors 'despite disagreement with their Frankish overlords, until 893' (Duchy page). The page does not date 888; unverified within the page budget.
Unchanged shape for 892-895: 893 Rainulf II poisoned, William the Pious made duke by Charles the Simple. Cliopatria stops in 895 although the duchy goes on (William d. 918, William II d. 926).

region.text: Charibert's realm 'included Toulouse, Cahors, Agen, Périgueux, and Saintes' and Gascony: 'Gascony and the southern fringe of Aquitaine proper'

ledger.note: 629: Dagobert I grants his half-brother Charibert II a subkingdom of Aquitaine with its capital at Toulouse. 'Charibert's realm included Toulouse, Cahors, Agen, Périgueux, and Saintes' and he 'added his possessions in Gascony'; reign from 18 October 629 (infobox). Duchy of Aquitaine page: Dagobert 'granted a subkingdom in southern Aquitaine to his younger brother', 'consisting of Gascony and the southern fringe of Aquitaine proper'.

region.text: Charibert's realm 'included Toulouse, Cahors, Agen, Périgueux, and Saintes' and Gascony: 'Gascony and the southern fringe of Aquitaine proper'

ledger.note: 632: Charibert II dies (8 April); 'Aquitaine passed again to Dagobert' and 'soon after that his infant son Chilperic was killed'. The Basques 'revolted again' after his death and were 'subdued by an army sent by Dagobert' in 635 (Duchy of Aquitaine page). No Aquitaine row in Cliopatria for 633-660: Frankish province.

region.text: the duchy as Cliopatria draws it from 674 (Loire to Pyrenees, 205 k km2), used for 661-673 where Cliopatria's own shapes are the Frankish heartland

ledger.note: c.660: the duchy appears. 'The first duke is on record under the name of Felix, and as having ruled from about 660'; it 'established itself as a quasi-independent realm within the Frankish empire' in the late 7th century (infobox: 'Independent duchy (late 7th century - 769)'). The page names no territory for Felix: the region is the 674 Cliopatria shape, read from Odo's 'Loire to the Pyrenees' (Odo page) and Gascony's 'personal union with Aquitaine from the 7th to the 9th century'.

region.text: Bourges, seized by Charles Martel, and the Berry on the Loire frontier

ledger.note: 731: Charles Martel crosses the Loire and takes Bourges. 'In 731, the Frankish leader Charles Martel, after defeating the Saxons' attacked; 'Charles Martel ransacked Aquitaine twice, seizing Bourges, too' (Odo page); 'crossed the Loire in 731 and looted much of Aquitaine' (Duchy page).

732: Odo, beaten by the Umayyads near Bordeaux, asks Charles Martel for help and gets it 'in exchange for accepting formal Frankish overlordship'; Charles and Odo's allies beat the Umayyads at Tours in 732 and 'expelled them from Aquitaine'. The page does not say whether Bourges stayed Frankish; Cliopatria's Frankish shape from 732 covers the whole duchy. The overlordship itself is a vassal tint for the Frankish dossier (kingdom-of-the-franks should carry the vassal_start).

region.text: the counts' towns of Bourges and Limoges

ledger.note: 735: Charles Martel attacks Hunald. 'Odo was succeeded by his son Hunald, who reverted to former independence' and 'In 735 and 736 Martel attacked Hunald and his allies, the counts of key Aquitanian towns such as Bourges and Limoges.'

region.text: the counts' towns of Bourges and Limoges

ledger.note: 736: the last dated attack of Charles Martel on Hunald ('In 735 and 736 Martel attacked...'). The page records no peace; Hunald 'retired to a monastery' leaving the duchy to Waifer, undated. The end year is the last dated campaign, not a treaty.

region.text: the duchy of Waifer, fought over for eight years

ledger.note: 760: Pepin the Short opens the War of Aquitaine. 'Following the full occupation of Septimania in 759, Pepin turned now his attention to Aquitaine, initiating a cyclical military campaign that lasted for eight years, i.e. the War of Aquitaine'; 'Waifer strenuously carried on an unequal struggle with the Carolingian Franks'. The page names no town; 760 is 759 + the page's order of events, the zone is the whole duchy.

768: Waifer is assassinated. 'Basque-Aquitanian self-rule temporarily came to a halt, definitely in 768 after the assassination of Waifer'; the Duchy page: 'his assassination in 768 marked the demise of Aquitaine's relative independence'.

region.text: Waifer's duchy, 'conquered by the Franks in 769'

ledger.note: 768: the Franks take the duchy. 'The autonomous and troublesome duchy of Aquitaine was conquered by the Franks in 769, after a series of revolts against their suzerainty' (Duchy page): 768 is the Aquitaine page's year and Cliopatria's (its Frankish shape grows in 768); 769 is the Duchy page's. Gascony stays apart as Cliopatria's Duchy of Gascony from 768.

region.text: 'Aquitaine proper, but also Gothia, Vasconia (Gascony) and the Carolingian possessions in Spain'

ledger.note: 781: Charlemagne makes his three-year-old son Louis king of Aquitaine. 'It included not only Aquitaine proper, but also Gothia, Vasconia (Gascony) and the Carolingian possessions in Spain as well', 'subordinated to the Carolingian king or (later) emperor'. A sub-kingdom: the Frankish dossier may prefer a lighter tint. Louis reigned to 814, then Pepin I (814-838) and Pepin II (chosen 838; in possession 845-852).

region.text: 'Poitou, Saintonge, and Angoumois in the northwest of the region'

ledger.counterpart: Rainulf I, count of Poitiers (new Duchy of Aquitaine)
ledger.note: 845: the treaty of Charles the Bald and Pepin II. 'By a treaty made in 845 between Charles the Bald and Pepin II, the kingdom had been diminished by the loss of Poitou, Saintonge, and Angoumois in the northwest of the region, which had been given to Rainulf I, count of Poitiers.' Kingdom page: 'from 845 to 852 Pepin II was in possession of the kingdom', and at Easter 848 at Limoges Charles was elected king.

minus.text: 'Aquitaine proper, but also Gothia, Vasconia (Gascony) and the Carolingian possessions in Spain'
'Poitou, Saintonge, and Angoumois in the northwest of the region'

ledger.note: 877: the kingdom ends. 'when, in 877, Louis became king of the Franks, Aquitaine was fully absorbed into the Frankish crown' (Louis the Stammerer had been king of Aquitaine from 866).

888: the duchy of the Poitevin counts is drawn as a state again. The page is silent on 888: it says the 'new Duchy of Aquitaine' stayed with Rainulf I's successors 'despite disagreement with their Frankish overlords, until 893'. The year and extent are Cliopatria's (204 k km2); the west-franks dossier of group eu-07 dates the break to 888 from a page not opened here.

893: 'Count Rainulf II was poisoned by order of King Charles III, or Charles the Simple. Charles then bestowed the duchy upon William the Pious, count of Auvergne, the founder of the abbey of Cluny'; William was 'succeeded in 918 by his nephew, Count William II, who died in 926'. Same duchy, new house (the Poitevin counts to the Auvergnat William): one colour.

895: Cliopatria's Aquitaine row ends, not the duchy. William the Pious (893-918) and William II (to 926) still hold it, and Cliopatria's next row is the Duchy of Aquitaine from 990 with the land inside the West Franks between. A bookkeeping end, confidence 1: the duchy-of-aquitaine dossier should be extended back by its owner or the gap filled.

wars.name: Battle of Toulouse (721)
wars.outcome: Odo 'inflicted a major defeat upon Al-Samh ibn Malik al-Khawlani at the Battle of Toulouse' on 9 June 721; no land changed.
wars.note: Duchy page: 'He inflicted on the Moors a crushing defeat at the Battle of Toulouse in 721.'

wars.name: Umayyad raid of 732 and Battle of Tours
wars.outcome: The Umayyads under Abd al-Rahman 'raided Vasconia, advanced towards Bordeaux and ransacked the city' and beat Odo near Bordeaux; Odo accepted Frankish overlordship for help and the alliance beat them at Tours, expelling them from Aquitaine. No lasting border change.
wars.note: Duchy page: Moors 'defeated Odo twice near Bordeaux'; raids 'as far north as Poitiers'. Tours is not on the Duchy page.

wars.name: Charles Martel's campaigns in Aquitaine
wars.outcome: Charles crossed the Loire in 731, 'ransacked Aquitaine twice, seizing Bourges', then in 735 and 736 attacked Hunald and the counts of Bourges and Limoges; Odo had accepted overlordship in 732. No dated partition.
wars.note: Duchy page for 735-736 and Hunald's 'former independence'.

wars.name: War of Aquitaine (Pepin the Short)

zones.text: the whole duchy, the page names no town

wars.outcome: After Pepin occupied Septimania (759) he fought 'a cyclical military campaign that lasted for eight years'; Waifer was assassinated in 768 and 'the autonomous and troublesome duchy of Aquitaine was conquered by the Franks in 769'.
wars.note: Pepin's forces 'destroyed up to 36 monasteries'. Eight years from 760 ends 768; the page's own start year is not given.

certainty.note: No treaty line in the period fixes a frontier of Aquitaine; the Loire frontier, the Pyrenees and the Septimanian edge are approximate. The 845 treaty's loss of Poitou, Saintonge and Angoumois is the one named division, and the page gives districts, not a line.

notes: Cliopatria rows: (1) aquitaine_661 (649 k km2) and aquitaine_666 (517 k km2) are the Frankish heartland, not Aquitaine: marked wrong, the 674 shape substituted; the Frankish row has 137 km2 for 661-665, so group eu-07's kingdom-of-the-franks dossier should take the 661-673 heartland back from Aquitaine. (2) Cliopatria has no Aquitaine for 633-660, 732-749 (the Frankish 732-749 shape covers the duchy, against the pages), 768-887 (Carolingian sub-kingdom 781-877 and Duchy of Gascony 768+ overlap) and 896-989. New keyframes aquitaine_732, _781, _845 fill 732-749 and 781-877; 768-780 and 878-887 stay empty. (3) The row ends 895 although the duchy continues to the 'Duchy of Aquitaine' row of 990: flag for the owner of duchy-of-aquitaine. (4) Pages disagree on when the Carolingian kingdom ended: 843 'ceased to have any relevance' (Aquitaine page) against 877 'fully absorbed' (Kingdom page); 877 is followed. (5) The Duchy page gives Gascony in personal union from the 7th to 9th century and Cliopatria's Duchy of Gascony starts 768: the Gascony overlap in 781-877 is for that group. (6) Unchecked within the page budget: 888 (Rainulf II's break, undated here), Hunald's retirement year, Waifer's accession, Felix's land; a gap filler should open 'Hunald I of Aquitaine', 'Waiofar', 'Lupus I of Aquitaine', 'Ranulf II of Aquitaine'. Gazetteer names lacking: Cahors, Agen, Périgueux, Saintes (places), used here through admin-1 departments or a radius. Vassal tint of Aquitaine under the Franks (732-749, 781-877) belongs on the Frankish dossier. Rulers not given: the pages give reigns only for 781-877 and not for the dukes.
